extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines and 30 subjects.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen. MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI. arXiv:2311.16502v4, 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was manually collected by a team of 50 college students who gathered multimodal questions from major textbooks, online resources, and lecture materials, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, major textbooks, lecture materials, and online resources.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators collected multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources, creating new questions where necessary, and annotated fields including the question, answer options, correct answer, image types, difficulty, and explanation. Quality control involved duplicate removal, format and typo checking by co-authors, difficulty categorization, and vetting by a secondary review team.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Suspected duplicates were reviewed by authors to eliminate duplications. Problems were distributed among co-authors for format and typo checking, and categorized into difficulty levels. A secondary review team vetted annotations, and ambiguities were collaboratively examined in team meetings.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and '90th percentile of skilled adults,' nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle; the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Monitoring the progress towards Expert AGI is of societal importance due to significant risks of job displacement and economic disruption.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The annotators should avoid collecting questions that contain any private information.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning; instrumental in developing next-generation multimodal foundation models and monitoring the progress towards Expert AGI.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step requires authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations are found. In the third and final stage... Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.
